Library Loading
```{r}
library(igraph)
library(ggraph)
library(msigdbr)
library(fgsea)

# Load the InWeb PPI database.
load(file='/home/projects/22140/exercise4.Rdata')
```



Set of proteins involved in Parkinson's Disease (PD).
```{r}

seeds <- c('PRKN', 'PINK1', 'LRRK2', 'VPS35', 'RAB32', 'GBA1', 'MAPT', 'SNCA', 'HLA-DRA', 'NR4A2', 'PARK7')
```


Extracting all connections with a confidence score >= 0.2
```{r}
connections_df <- inWeb[inWeb$inweb_cs >= 0.2,
                        c("from", "to", "inweb_cs")]

# Creating the graph with the data
g <- graph_from_data_frame(connections_df, directed = FALSE)
plot(g)
```

Virtual pulldown is performed in two steps: first, we extract the sub-graph, and then we filter the virtual pulldown.

Using the ego() function we can extract all the first degree neighbors.
```{r}
seed_neigbors <- ego(
  graph = g,
  order = 1,
  nodes = V(g)[name %in% seeds],
  mode = "all"
)
```

as_ids() is used to convert each vertex sequence into a regular vector of IDs, and unlist() flattens the list of vectors into a single vector containing all neigbors of all seeds.
```{r}
sub_nodes_names <- unique(unlist(lapply(seed_neigbors, as_ids)))
```


The subnetwork based on a set of node ids is extracted.
```{r}
g_sub <- induced_subgraph(g, vids = V(g)[name %in% sub_nodes_names])
```


Filtering the virtual pulldown.
```{r}
filter_virtual_pulldown <- function(subGraph, parentGraph, cutoff) {
  if (is.null(V(subGraph)$name) || is.null(V(parentGraph)$name))
    stop("both graphs must have vertex 'name attributes.")
  
  mode <- "all"
  
  vn <- V(subGraph)$name
  
  # Degree in the full graph.
  deg_full <- degree(parentGraph, v = vn, mode = mode)
  
  # Degree inside the subgraph.
  deg_internal <- degree(subGraph, mode = mode)
  
  res <- data.frame(
    node = vn,
    deg_internal = deg_internal,
    deg_full = deg_full,
    frac_internal = ifelse(deg_full > 0, deg_internal / deg_full, NA_real_),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
    
  # Keep nodes that pass the cutoff.
  nodes_to_keep <- res$node[!is.na(res$frac_internal) & res$frac_internal >= cutoff]
  
  # A new subgraph contains the nodes that meet the criteria.
  filteredSubGraph <- induced_subgraph(subGraph, vids = V(subGraph)[name %in% nodes_to_keep])

  V(filteredSubGraph)$frac_internal <- res$frac_internal[match(V(filteredSubGraph)$name, res$node)]
  
  filteredSubGraph
  
}
```




```{r}
cuts <- c(0, 0.2, 0.5, 1)
# function to check the size of the network
net_size <- function(g) c(nodes = vcount(g), edges = ecount(g))
# run the filtering function and collect sizes
filtered <- lapply(cuts, function(ct) filter_virtual_pulldown(g_sub, g, cutoff = ct))

sizes <- t(sapply(filtered, net_size))
rownames(sizes) <- paste0("cutoff_", cuts)
sizes
```

A 0.2 cutoff is applied to extract the first degree neighbors; after the 0.2 cutoff, we are only left with few proteins, resulting in a much less informative plot to further extract potential subclusters.
We are only keeping the nodes whose 20% or more of the total connections lie inside the subgraph.

Visualizing the network
```{r}
g_filt <- filter_virtual_pulldown(g_sub, g, 0.2)

is_seed <- V(g_filt)$name %in% seeds
V(g_filt)$role <- ifelse(is_seed, "seed", "neighbor")

ggraph(g_filt, layout = "fr") + 
  geom_edge_link() + 
  geom_node_point(aes(color = role))
```


Finding potential subclusers 
```{r}
cl <- cluster_louvain(g_filt, weights = NULL, resolution = 0.4)

V(g_filt)$cluster <- factor(membership(cl))

ggraph(g_filt, layout = "fr") + 
  geom_edge_link() + 
  geom_node_point(aes(color = cluster))
```


```{r}
n_clusters <- sort(table(V(g_filt)$cluster), decreasing = TRUE)
n_clusters
```

All nodes of the network will be the universe for the overrepesentation analysis.
```{r}
BP_df = msigdbr(species = "human", category = "C5", subcategory = "BP")

BP_list = split(x = BP_df$gene_symbol, f = BP_df$gs_name)
background <- V(g_filt)$name
```


ORA for cluster 1 (n = 251 genes)
```{r}
target <- V(g_filt)$name[V(g_filt)$cluster == 1]

BP_gsea <- fora(BP_list, target, background)

top10_bp <- head(BP_gsea[order(BP_gsea$padj, BP_gsea$pval), ], 10)
print(as.data.frame(top10_bp), row.names = FALSE, right = FALSE)
```

Gene with the highest betweenness centrality

```{r}
largest_cluster <- 1

g_largest <- induced_subgraph(g_filt, vids = V(g_filt)[cluster == largest_cluster])

bw <- betweenness(g_largest, directed = FALSE, normalized = TRUE)
bw_max <- max(bw, na.rm = TRUE)
top_gene <- names(bw)[bw == bw_max]
top_gene
```
